text_map.central_idea: The speaker recalls a calm, courteous carriage ride with Death. It passes the stages of life and ends at the grave. From the vantage of 'centuries' later, she shows that death has changed her sense of time, making eternity feel briefer than the single day she understood where she was going.
text_map.speaker_or_narrator: A first-person speaker, apparently already dead, looking back on the day Death called for her and the journey that followed.

structure_and_shifts.from: the speaker's busy life, in which she 'could not stop'
structure_and_shifts.to: Death's polite intervention, which begins the journey
the close of day, signaling life's end

structure_and_shifts.quote: We paused before a house that seemed
Since then 't is centuries; but each
structure_and_shifts.to: a timeless present that reveals the speaker's posthumous perspective

devices.function: Presents Death as a courteous gentleman caller, which softens its terror.
The repeated 'We passed' gives the ride a steady, procession-like movement through life's stages.
The grave is pictured as a house, its roof hardly rising above the earth.

devices.quote: We passed the fields of gazing grain,
devices.function: Ripened grain suggests maturity and a living world that watches as the speaker passes.
Centuries feel shorter than one day, which shows how eternity distorts time.

skills_supported.why_supported: 'gazing grain' works literally as ripened crops and figuratively as a living world that watches the speaker pass.
skills_supported.quote: We passed the fields of gazing grain,

skills_supported.why_supported: Several passages bear on time, so students can choose the best evidence for a claim about how death distorts time.

items.stem: In context, the phrase describing the fields ([[r1]]) works on two levels at once, suggesting both

options.text: a menacing, shadowed landscape and the speaker's growing terror as Death hurries her to the grave
options.label: wrong_tone
options.why: The ride is unhurried and calm. Death 'knew no haste', and nothing suggests terror.
options.evidence_quote: We slowly drove, he knew no haste,

options.text: a farm the carriage is heading toward and the comfortable new home in which the speaker will settle
options.label: literal_for_figurative
options.why: The carriage passes the fields rather than stopping there. The only 'home' it reaches is a grave, described as a mound in the earth.

options.text: a literal field of ripened grain and a living world that watches passively as the speaker goes by
options.label: correct
options.why: The grain is literally mature, at a late stage of growth. 'Gazing' also makes it an onlooker that stays behind while the carriage carries the speaker past life's scenes.
options.evidence_quote: We passed the fields of gazing grain,

options.text: a harvest the speaker means to gather and the reward she expects for her lifetime of earthly labor
options.label: reversal
options.why: The speaker has already given up her work. She will gather nothing, and she simply passes the fields.
options.evidence_quote: My labor, and my leisure too,

items.stem: A student claims that the poem shows death changing the speaker's sense of time, so that vast spans come to feel brief. Which of the following quotations provides the strongest evidence for this claim?

options.text: "We passed the school where children played, / Their lessons scarcely done"
options.label: wrong_function
options.why: This image shows a stage of life the speaker passes. It is about what she leaves behind, not about how she now perceives time.
options.evidence_quote: We passed the school where children played,

options.text: "We paused before a house that seemed / A swelling of the ground"
options.label: too_narrow
options.why: These lines identify where the journey ends, at the grave. They say nothing about how long spans of time feel to the speaker.
options.evidence_quote: We paused before a house that seemed

options.text: "We slowly drove, he knew no haste, / And I had put away / My labor"
options.label: partially_right
options.why: These lines describe the slow pace of the ride itself. They do not show long periods of time feeling short afterward.
options.evidence_quote: We slowly drove, he knew no haste,

options.text: "Since then 't is centuries; but each / Feels shorter than the day"
options.label: correct
options.why: Here the speaker says that centuries feel shorter than a single day. This states directly that, after death, vast spans of time feel brief.
options.evidence_quote: Since then 't is centuries; but each

evidence_quotes: Since then 't is centuries; but each
